name: Empire Mimikatz sekurlsa::logonpasswords – In-Memory Credential Dumping via PowerShell
root_cause: An Empire C2 agent running under user 'pgustavo' on WORKSTATION5 executed an in-memory PowerShell payload (delivered as a Base64-encoded command) that reflectively loaded Mimikatz-equivalent code using native Win32 API calls (OpenProcess / ReadProcessMemory) to access lsass.exe memory and dump plaintext credentials and NTLM hashes (sekurlsa::logonpasswords). The agent maintained a persistent HTTP callback to the C2 listener at 10.10.10.5:80. Post-dump, the agent issued 'whoami /user' to enumerate the current identity.
remediation_actions: Isolate WORKSTATION5.theshire.local from the network immediately to terminate the active C2 channel to 10.10.10.5:80.
Terminate the malicious powershell.exe process (PID 1648) on WORKSTATION5.
Assume all credentials cached on WORKSTATION5 are compromised; force a domain-wide password reset starting with privileged accounts.
Reset Kerberos tickets (run klist purge) and revoke NTLM sessions for THESHIRE\pgustavo and any accounts whose hashes may have been dumped.
Block outbound TCP to 10.10.10.5:80 at the network perimeter and investigate the C2 host.
Review all lateral movement from WORKSTATION5 since 2020-08-07T14:32Z for pass-the-hash or pass-the-ticket activity.
Enable Credential Guard on Windows 10+ endpoints to prevent future lsass memory reads.
Add a SIEM alert for Sysmon EventID 10 where TargetImage contains lsass.exe and GrantedAccess includes 0x0010 (VM_READ).
